providers.name: BSNL Wings

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: The number callers dial. Used only to label the inbound trunk.

fields.label: SIP username
fields.help: From the Wings SIP credentials screen.

fields.label: SIP password
fields.help: Keep this private. Stored in data/trunk.json.

fields.label: Registration URI
fields.help: Mandatory for Wings. Usually sip:<username>@ims.bsnl.in:5060

purchase.summary: Wings is BSNL's SIP/IMS service. Buy a Wings number, enable SIP credentials, then register Asterisk to ims.bsnl.in.
steps: Open the Wings app or BSNL Wings portal and sign in.
Buy or port a number for inbound calls.
Enable SIP / IMS credentials and copy username, password, and registrar.
If BSNL gives extra proxy IPs, add them under extra match IPs below.

tips: Wings is registration-based. Do not skip the registration URI.
Allow UDP 5060 and your RTP range (default 10000-20000) on the firewall.

providers.name: Jio SIP trunk

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Enterprise DID Jio assigned you.

fields.label: SIP username (if issued)
fields.help: Leave blank when Jio authenticates by IP only.

fields.label: Registration URI
fields.help: Only if Jio asked you to REGISTER. Most Jio trunks are IP-based.

purchase.summary: Jio enterprise SIP trunks are usually IP-authenticated. Give Jio this server's public IP, then match their signalling IPs inbound.
steps: Talk to Jio Business / JioMeet enterprise for a SIP trunk.
Share this PBX public IP and ask for their signalling IP ranges.
Paste those ranges into Extra match IPs if they differ from the defaults.

tips: IP-based trunks need accurate match= CIDRs or inbound INVITEs are rejected.
Ask Jio whether they send calls from multiple SBC IPs.

providers.name: Airtel SIP trunk

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Airtel business SIP / PRIs-over-SIP are typically IP-authenticated from Airtel SBCs.
steps: Order an Airtel business SIP trunk.
Give them this server's public IP.
Copy the SBC IPs they send in the welcome letter into match=.

tips: Confirm codec: ulaw/alaw is what this skeleton allows.

providers.name: Tata Tele SIP

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

steps: Order a SIP trunk.

providers.name: Exotel

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Buy a virtual number in the Exotel dashboard, then create a SIP trunk / endpoint.
steps: Create an Exotel account.
Buy a number in your city.
Create SIP credentials and paste them here.

tips: Exotel IPs change; add every signalling IP they list.

providers.name: Plivo — Outbound

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: E.164 number from Plivo, for example +14155550100.

fields.label: SIP Username
fields.help: Username from the Plivo Credentials List. Required for the SIP credentials authentication method.

fields.label: SIP Password
fields.help: Password from the Plivo Credentials List. Required for the SIP credentials authentication method.

fields.label: Registration / Client URI
fields.help: Usually leave blank. Enter this only for a Plivo product setup that explicitly asks for a SIP registration URI. Example: sip:<auth-id>@<termination-domain>:5060.

purchase.summary: Use a Plivo outbound trunk to send calls from this PBX/AI agent to PSTN numbers.
steps: In Plivo Console, create an Outbound Zentrunk.
Attach either a Credentials List or an IP ACL. A DID, SIP username, and SIP password are normally required for credential-based outbound calls.
Copy the Termination SIP Domain into the SIP Host / FQDN URI field.
Enter the same Credentials List username and password below.
Use UDP/TCP on port 5060, or TLS on port 5061 for Secure Trunking.

tips: Use the Plivo Termination SIP Domain, for example xxxxxxxxxxxx.zt.plivo.com, as the SIP Host / FQDN URI.
SIP Username and SIP Password come from the Plivo Credentials List, not the Plivo API Auth ID/Auth Token.
An outbound trunk does not send inbound calls to this PBX. Create an inbound trunk for incoming calls.
Match Plivo signaling ranges below to accept provider traffic; TLS uses signaling port 5061.

providers.name: Plivo — Inbound

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: E.164 number from Plivo, for example +14155550100.

fields.label: Origination Auth Username
fields.help: Optional. Only enter this if Authentication is enabled on the Plivo Origination URI. To use it, select SIP credentials above.

fields.label: Origination Auth Password
fields.help: Optional. Leave blank unless Authentication is enabled on the Plivo Origination URI.

purchase.summary: Use a Plivo inbound trunk to send calls from Plivo numbers to this PBX or AI agent. Inbound delivery uses an Origination URI; it does not require REGISTER or a username/password by default.
steps: In Plivo Console, create an Inbound Zentrunk.
Create a Primary Origination URI pointing to this PBX's public FQDN/IP and port, for example sip:pbx.example.com:5060.
Leave Origination authentication off unless you need it. When off, do not enter a username/password.
Enter the E.164 DID below and assign it to the inbound trunk.
Allow Plivo signalling and media IP ranges in the match list below.

tips: Enter the public SIP URI of this PBX, for example sip:pbx.example.com or your-server-ip. This is the Primary Origination URI you give Plivo.
Do not enter Plivo outbound credentials for a normal inbound trunk; Plivo forwards calls to the Origination URI.
Enable Origination auth only if you intend to authenticate Plivo's INVITEs. If using SIP credentials mode, the username and password below become required.
Create a separate outbound trunk when calls must leave through Plivo.
Default inbound signaling is UDP/TCP on port 5060; Secure Trunking uses TLS on port 5061.

providers.name: Twilio Elastic SIP

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

fields.label: Termination username
fields.help: From Elastic SIP Trunk termination, if using credential lists.

fields.label: Registration URI
fields.help: Twilio trunks are usually IP ACL, not REGISTER.

purchase.summary: Create an Elastic SIP Trunk in Twilio, add this PBX IP to the ACL, and buy a number on that trunk.
steps: Open Twilio Console → Elastic SIP Trunking.
Create a trunk. Add origination URI sip:<your-public-ip>.
Add your public IP to the IP ACL (or a credential list).
Buy a number and assign it to the trunk.

tips: Put the Twilio origination SIP domain in Host FQDN if they gave you one.
Keep match= in sync with Twilio's published signalling ranges.

providers.name: Telnyx

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Create a Telnyx SIP connection (IP or credentials), buy a number, attach it.
steps: Create a SIP connection.
Allow this PBX IP or set credentials.
Order a number and assign the connection.

tips: Telnyx can do credential auth; fill username/password if you chose that.

providers.name: Vonage (Nexmo)

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Buy a Vonage virtual number and point SIP interconnect at this PBX.
steps: Create a Vonage account.
Buy a number.
Configure SIP forwarding to this host.

tips: Confirm the interconnect region; host_fqdn may be regional.

providers.name: VoIP.ms

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Create a VoIP.ms sub-account, pick a POP close to you, buy a DID.
steps: Create a sub-account with a strong password.
Set device type to Asterisk.
Order a DID and route it to the sub-account.

tips: Use the POP hostname (dallas, montreal, london, …) as Host FQDN.

providers.name: SIP.US

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Sign up at SIP.US, create a trunk, buy DIDs.
steps: Create a trunk in the portal.
Copy username/password.
Assign DIDs to the trunk.

tips: gw1 and gw2 are both valid; use the one they assigned.

providers.name: Callcentric

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Register at Callcentric, create a SIP account, optional DID.
steps: Create an account.
Note the 1777 username.
Buy a DID if you need inbound PSTN.

tips: Callcentric publishes several match IPs — keep them all.

providers.name: DIDWW

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Buy a DIDWW number, create a voice IN trunk pointing at this PBX IP.
steps: Create a voice IN trunk with your public IP.
Buy a DID and assign the trunk.

tips: DIDWW signalling hosts are listed in their docs — paste extras below.

providers.name: Flowroute

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Provider-assigned DID or phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550100.

purchase.summary: Add this PBX IP as a Flowroute route, buy DIDs, set the preferred POP.
steps: Add an IP alias in Flowroute.
Order DIDs.
Set inbound route to that alias.

tips: Outbound often uses a tech prefix; username can hold that prefix.

providers.name: Custom / other provider

fields.label: Provider Number / DID (E.164)
fields.help: Number callers dial. Configuration only.

fields.label: Registration URI
fields.help: Required for REGISTER-based PBX (like Wings). Leave empty for IP authentication.

purchase.summary: Use this when your carrier is not listed. Copy host, credentials, and signalling IPs from their SIP sheet.
steps: Get the SIP spec from the provider (host, port, auth type, codecs).
If they REGISTER, fill Registration URI as sip:user@host.
If they authenticate by IP, leave Registration URI empty and list every signalling CIDR.

tips: match= must list the IPs the provider sends INVITEs from.
ulaw and alaw are enabled on the trunk template.
